title: Knee Arthritis: Weather, Hot or Cold Packs, Diet, Sleep and Other Questions Patients Ask
metaDescription: Does cold weather worsen knee arthritis? Hot or ice pack? Which food helps? Will it spread? Honest answers to the everyday questions patients ask.
intro: These are the questions patients ask us most, including ones they are shy to ask. Short answers: weather can affect how your knee feels but does not cause arthritis, heat and ice can both help, no special food cures it, and exercise does not wear the knee out.

sections.heading: Does cold or rainy weather make knee arthritis worse?
sections.body: Many people do feel more pain when air pressure drops, for example before rain, says Versus Arthritis. Weather affects how the knee feels but it does not cause arthritis, and not everyone notices it. Keep the knee warm and keep moving.

sections.heading: Should I use a hot pack or an ice pack?
sections.body: Both can help. Warmth, such as a hot-water bottle or heat pack wrapped in a towel, can ease pain and stiffness. For a swollen knee, an ice pack wrapped in a towel for up to 20 minutes every couple of hours can help. Never put heat or ice directly on the skin.

sections.heading: Is there a special diet for knee arthritis?
sections.body: No food has been proven to cure it. Versus Arthritis says body weight matters more than any particular food. Some people notice that certain foods affect their symptoms. A balanced diet that helps you reach a healthy weight is sensible advice.

sections.heading: Do supplements and oil massage work?
sections.body: Glucosamine and chondroitin are no longer prescribed on the NHS because evidence of benefit is weak. Gentle massage or warm oil can feel soothing, and there is no harm in it if the skin is healthy, but it will not repair the knee.

sections.heading: Will exercise wear out my knee?
sections.body: No. This is a common myth. The right exercise strengthens the knee and improves symptoms, and too much rest makes the knee stiffer. Versus Arthritis also says arthritis is not simply wear and tear.

sections.heading: Why is my knee worse at night or after sitting?
sections.body: Stiffness after sitting is typical and usually eases once you start moving. Severe arthritis can disturb sleep, and regular exercise may help sleep. If night pain is severe or new, have it checked.

sections.heading: Will it spread to my other joints?
sections.body: No. Arthritis does not spread through the body, though a painful knee can overload the other knee, the hip or the back as you walk differently.

faqs.q: Can cold weather cause knee arthritis?
faqs.a: No. Weather can make it feel worse but does not cause it.

faqs.q: Is heat or cold better for knee arthritis?
faqs.a: Heat for stiffness and ache, ice for swelling.
A family history raises the risk, but it is not certain.

faqs.q: Can I drive with knee arthritis?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if you can control the pedals comfortably. After a knee replacement the NHS advises waiting at least 6 weeks for a total replacement.
